subproblem.title: Projected lattice cells of ℝ^{N+1}: vertical cells contribute 0, horizontal cells are isometric copies of grid cubes of ℝ^N (parent steps 5(c) and 9)
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d] (Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω), d = exteriorDerivative); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm: |α|² = Σ_I α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(d−1)})² over strictly increasing I); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 denotes the standard basis vector of the respective space; castSucc : Fin P → Fin (P + 1) and last = Fin.last P. Let N ∈ ℕ, ρ ∈ ℝ, let p : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^N be a continuous linear map with (py)_i = y_{castSucc i} for all y and i ∈ Fin N, let z ∈ ℤ^{N+1} and let ι : Fin N → Fin (N + 1) be strictly increasing. Put F̃ := {y ∈ ℝ^{N+1} : for every i, ρz_i ≤ y_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) if i ∈ range ι, and y_i = ρz_i if i ∉ range ι} (the cell of the cubical grid of side ρ at z spanned by the directions ι) and G := {x ∈ ℝ^N : ρz_{castSucc i} ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_{castSucc i} + 1) for every i ∈ Fin N}. (a) If last = Fin.last N ∈ range ι ('vertical' cell), then ∫_{F̃} ω(py)(pe_{ι(0)}, …, pe_{ι(N−1)}) dHᴺ(y) = 0 for every N-form ω on ℝ^N (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) N). (b) If last ∉ range ι ('horizontal' cell), then ∫_{F̃} ω(py)(pe_{ι(0)}, …, pe_{ι(N−1)}) dHᴺ(y) = ∫_G ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) dHᴺ(x) for every N-form ω on ℝ^N, and every x ∈ G equals py for some y ∈ F̃. (All integrals are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (p : Euclid (N + 1) →L[ℝ] Euclid N) (z : Fin (N + 1) → ℤ) (ι : Fin N → Fin (N + 1)), (∀ (y : Euclid (N + 1)) (i : Fin N), p y i = y (Fin.castSucc i)) → StrictMono ι → (Fin.last N ∈ Set.range ι → ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) N, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (N + 1) | ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (i ∈ Set.range ι → ρ * z i ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ ρ * (z i + 1)) ∧ (i ∉ Set.range ι → y i = ρ * z i)}, ω (p y) (fun k => p (EuclideanSpace.single (ι k) (1 : ℝ))) ∂μHE[N] = 0) ∧ (Fin.last N ∉ Set.range ι → (∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) N, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (N + 1) | ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (i ∈ Set.range ι → ρ * z i ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ ρ * (z i + 1)) ∧ (i ∉ Set.range ι → y i = ρ * z i)}, ω (p y) (fun k => p (EuclideanSpace.single (ι k) (1 : ℝ))) ∂μHE[N] = ∫ x in {x : Euclid N | ∀ i : Fin N, ρ * z (Fin.castSucc i) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ ρ * (z (Fin.castSucc i) + 1)}, ω x (fun k => EuclideanSpace.single k (1 : ℝ)) ∂μHE[N]) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid N, (∀ i : Fin N, ρ * z (Fin.castSucc i) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ ρ * (z (Fin.castSucc i) + 1)) → ∃ y : Euclid (N + 1), (∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (i ∈ Set.range ι → ρ * z i ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ ρ * (z i + 1)) ∧ (i ∉ Set.range ι → y i = ρ * z i)) ∧ p y = x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5(c) and 9 of the parent-supplied proof (if P ∈ range ι_p one of the vectors is p(e_P) = 0 and the term vanishes; otherwise range ι_p = {0, …, P − 1}, p e_{ι_p(k)} = e_k, and p maps F̃_p isometrically onto the cube G_{z'}, so the two integrals agree; and G_{z'} = p(F̃_p)). Tools: Mathlib ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_coord_zero (via the alternating map ω(py)), Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (μHE[N].map j = μHE[N].restrict (range j) for an isometry j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1}), Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map.
1. The images of the basis vectors. For j ∈ Fin (N+1) and i ∈ Fin N, (p e_j)_i = (e_j)_{castSucc i}, which is 1 if j = castSucc i and 0 otherwise. Hence p e_{castSucc k} = e_k for k ∈ Fin N, and p e_last = 0 because castSucc i ≠ last for all i.
2. Part (a). Let ι(k₀) = last. Then the k₀-th argument of the tuple (pe_{ι(0)}, …, pe_{ι(N−1)}) is p e_last = 0 (step 1), so for every y the multilinear map ω(py) vanishes on this tuple (map_coord_zero). The integrand is the zero function on ℝ^{N+1}, and the integral is 0.
3. Part (b), ι = castSucc. Assume last ∉ range ι. If N = 0, then ι = castSucc trivially (both are the empty map Fin 0 → Fin 1); F̃ is then the single point with last coordinate ρz_last, G = ℝ⁰ is a point, and steps 4–5 below apply unchanged. For N ≥ 1, a strictly increasing ι : Fin N → Fin (N+1) satisfies ι(k) ≥ k (induction on k). Moreover ι(N−1) ≤ N, and ι(N−1) ≠ N = last, so ι(N−1) ≤ N − 1; and for k < N − 1, ι(k) < ι(k+1) gives by downward induction ι(k) ≤ k. Hence ι(k) = k for all k, i.e. ι = castSucc. Consequently range ι = {j : j ≠ last}, the integrand is y ↦ h(y) := ω(py)(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) by step 1, and F̃ = {y : ρz_{castSucc i} ≤ y_{castSucc i} ≤ ρ(z_{castSucc i} + 1) for all i ∈ Fin N, and y_last = ρz_last}.
4. The isometric embedding. Define j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1} by j(x)_{castSucc i} := x_i (i ∈ Fin N) and j(x)_last := ρz_last. Then |j(x) − j(x')|² = Σ_i (x_i − x'_i)² = |x − x'|², so j is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding; and p(j(x)) = x by the defining formula of p. By the description of F̃ in step 3, j(G) ⊆ F̃; conversely, if y ∈ F̃ then x := py satisfies x_i = y_{castSucc i}, so x ∈ G, and y = j(x) because the coordinates castSucc i agree and y_last = ρz_last. Thus j(G) = F̃. In particular every x ∈ G equals p(j(x)) with j(x) ∈ F̃, which is the last claim of (b).
5. Change of variables. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, μHE[N].map j = μHE[N].restrict (range j); with MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and the injectivity of j, (μHE[N].restrict G).map j = (μHE[N].map j).restrict (j(G)) = μHE[N].restrict (j(G) ∩ range j) = μHE[N].restrict (j(G)). Hence, by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (valid for every function), ∫_{F̃} h dHᴺ = ∫_{j(G)} h dHᴺ = ∫_G h∘j dHᴺ = ∫_G ω(p(j(x)))(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) dHᴺ(x) = ∫_G ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) dHᴺ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: p e_{castSucc k} = e_k and p e_last = 0.
Vertical cells: a zero argument makes the integrand vanish identically.
Horizontal cells: a strictly increasing ι avoiding last is castSucc, and F̃ = j(G) for the isometric embedding j(x) = (x, ρz_last) with p∘j = id.
Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure turns ∫_{j(G)} h dHᴺ into ∫_G h∘j dHᴺ; p∘j = id gives the cube integral and G = p(F̃).

audit.reason: Vertical integrands vanish through a zero argument. A strictly increasing horizontal index is castSucc, giving an explicit affine isometry between the cube and cell and the required lifting property. MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map justifies arbitrary Bochner integrands. The proof covers N = 0 and every real ρ.
